info.description: Documentation for other versions: - V1.1 - V1.0 ### Key Changes in V2 #### Authentication - Authentication is performed via an OAuth2 Client Credentials Grant - Retailers are still identified by their `menu_integration_key` - Updated compound fields - `items[].compounds[].type` contains additional supported types e.g., `thca`, `cbdv`, `cbn` - `items[] contains `.total_thc` and `total_cbd` fields for summary cannabinoid #### Inbound Request Bodies - The `variant.id` field is now required - The `variant.price` field is now expected to be submitted as an integer of minor currency units - There must be at least one member of the `variants[]` array on items - Fields that have fallen into disuse have been removed from inbound request bodies: - `items[].batchId` - `items[].parentBatchId` - `items[].sku` - `items[].variants[].price_includes_tax` - `items[].variants[].tax_rate` - `items[].variants[].batchId` - `items[].variants[].parentBatchId` - `items[].variants[].sku` - A camel case convention has been adopted for all fields - Updated Compound fields - `items[].compounds[].type` enum now contains detailed cannabinoid types - e.g., `thca`, `cbdv`, `cbn`, etc. See schema for full list of supported types - `items[] contains `.total_thc` and `total_cbd` fields for summary cannabinoid information in the same structure as ``items[].compounds[]` #### Outbound Response Bodies - `items[].external_key` and `items[].variants[].external_key` are now serialized as `id`, carrying the same `id` value that was originally submitted to the API. - `items[].category` is now serialized as `type` - `items[].variants[].stock_quantity` is now serialized as `inventoryLevel` - Fields not considered relevant have been removed from outbound response bodies: - `items[].brand_id` - `items[].category` - `items[].dispensary_id` - `items[].pickup_override` - `items[].product_id` - `items[].sort_order` - `items[].staff_pick_order` - `items[].strain_id` - `items[].strain_key` - A camel case convention has been adopted for all fields #### Inventory Management - `items[].variants[]` must contain at least one entry in `POST` and `PUT requests`. Thus it is no longer possible to delete menu items by submitting an empty array of `variants[]`. Use the `DELETE` method instead. ### Overview This document describes how the system of record for a dispensary menu can be integrated for near-real-time menu updates on leafly.com. To make an update to the menu, the system of record should make an HTTP request to the menu integration URL using one of the specified methods below. The request should have a payload containing the menu items formatted in JSON. It is expected that when menu items are edited in the system of record or when inventory levels for a menu item change, that system will make these calls to update the menu on Leafly in near-real-time. ### Leafly Order API Integration Integrating with the Leafly Order API to manage Leafly orders in your point-of-sale system requires you to integrate to V2.0 of this Menu API. ### Latency Be aware that the effects of menu updates submitted through the API are not instantaneously visible, either on the consumer-facing site or through subsequent `GET` requests (when applicable). Background processing must occur that takes an indeterminate amount of time varying with system load. In the sandbox environment this is likely not more than about two and half minutes, while in the production environment this is likely not more than about five minutes. These intervals between submission and impact can be faster or slower depending on external factors. ### Tips and Best Practices #### Sync Frequency - **Initial Syncs or Reactivations**: Best achieved with a `POST` of a full menu with all items. - **Daily Syncs**: A full menu sync should be received by `POST` once per day, with `PUT` or `DELETE` updates accounting for individual item changes throughout the day. #### Inventory Management - **Item Publishing**: Items are published to the consumer site automatically if they're received via the API with inventory associated. If no inventory is provided, they'll be imported but unpublished (i.e., visible in the Leafly Menu Manager backend but not visible to shoppers on leafly.com) - **Availability Thresholds**: These are not currently supported via API, however there are toggles within each reatiler's Integreation Settings UI that can be used to set global or category-specific low inventory thresholds for hiding items. #### Data Standardization - **Strains**: If strain information is absent the value `null` should be submitted rather than `"NA"`. Transmitting `"NA"` will match items to the 'El-na' strain strain in the Leafly Strain Database. A post-ingestion job will attempt to match items to strains based on product name and descriptive content. - **Cannabinoids**: If cannabinoid information is absent the value `null` should be submitted rather than `0`. Transmitting `0` results in a display of `"0mg"` to shoppers rather than the preferable `"unknown"` - **Product Descriptions**: Do not submit product descriptions containing markup, all product descriptions should be submitted as plain text. ### Treatment of Medically Flagged Items Confusion at times arises about how the distinction of medical and non-medical variants influences the resulting menu on Leafly.com Generally, in the case of dual-licensed retailers (that is, retailers dealing in _both_ medical and recreational cannabis), sending a menu where all variants are homogeneously marked as `medical: true` or `medical: false` will result in separate but identical medical and recreational menus for the retailer on the consumer-facing site. Further for dual-licensed retailers, transmitting a menu containing a heterogenous mix of `medical: true` and `medical: false` variants is understood to mean the medically flagged items are restricted to medically privileged consumers, and that the non-medically flagged items are available to anyone who should want to buy them. Thus when such a menu is received, the `medical: true` items will be isolated to the retailer's medical menu, and the `medical: false` items will appear on both menus. In the case of recreational-only or medical-only retailers, the `medical` designation is generally considered to be a non-sequitur, and is ignored. ### Preparing for Production Separate production OAuth2 credentials must be obtained to utilize the production endpoints. Please coordinate production deployments with our Parnter Ops Team at partners@leafly.com. #### Certification Checklist Graudating from sandbox to production requires verifying the logged activity of your integration meets certain behavioral criteria: - **Correct Requests** - Integration client successfully authenticates to the API - Successful (200-level) responses are being solicted from the Menu API. If errors are present they're corrected on subsequent requests. - Request signatures indicate the presence of an automated application and not the use of manual tools (e.g., postman or curl) - **Menu Sync Frequency Profile** - **Option 1 (Recommended)**: - `POST` - Full menu updates across items at a cadence of once per day - `PUT` - Submission of item updates individually or in batches - `DELETE` - Removal of items from Leafly menus - **Option 2**: - `POST` - Submission of full menu syncs multiple times per hour - **Item Field Validation**: - Consistent use of items' `id` fields - Variants contain inventory that reflect most items are in stock - Strain values are set to `null` when absent - Cannabinoid values are set to `null` when absent - Values for fields generally sensible ### Getting Help For technical issues with the API or questions regarding this documentation, please contact API Support at api-support@leafly.com For access requests, production ramp-up, or other operational questions, please contact our Partner Ops Team at partners@leafly.com.
info.title: Leafly Menu Integration

OAuth2ClientCredentials.description:
The Leafly Menu API V2 uses OAuth 2 with the client credentials flow for inbound requests.
  The token url for the sandbox environment is `https://sso-sandbox.leafly.io/token`

menu_integration_key.name: menu_integration_key
menu_integration_key.description:
Each Leafly storefront will have a unique, Leafly generated key. You will use this key in
your request parameters to indicate which storefront you are pushing data in for.

get.description:
When you make an HTTP GET to the integration URL in the sandbox, the full
menu is returned. This method is only permitted in the sandbox environment;
an HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed response will be returned in other environments.
The schema is subject to change and this endpoint is provided only to aid in
development. Solutions should not rely on the availability of nor presented
schema of this endpoint.

post.description: Permits bulk update of a menu, using id to determine if changes are inserts or updates. Updates existing items that have a matching `id`. Inserts items if no matching `id` exists. Items not present in the post body are deleted from the Leafly menu. All items in the posted payload must have a unique value for `id`.

400.description: Bad Request. Malformed or invalid data. Confirm that all items have a unique `id`

put.description: Permits bulk updates of a menu, using `id` to determine if items are inserts or updates. Updates existing items that have a matching `id`. Inserts items if no matching `id` exists. Does not delete items. All items in the posted payload must have a unique value for `id`.

400.description: Bad Request. Malformed or invalid data. Confirm that all items have a unique `id`

delete.description: Deletes elements matching the `id`s provided in the body.

get.description:
Provides the status of a dispensary's menu integration, including summary
statistics for the dispensary menu.
